Treatment summary
The patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with a complaint of right knee pain and swelling.
The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported knee findings, and the presentation fits the force described.
Over the course of ten visits, the patient received physical therapy, activity modification, and anti-inflammatory
management. Treatment ran somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury, largely due to a gradual rate of
improvement in range of motion and strength. Examination revealed effusion and tenderness along the medial joint
line, which support the reported injury, while ligament stability testing and neurovascular assessment were within
normal limits. The patient mentioned a minor strain to the same knee area many years ago, which had resolved
completely without lasting limitation. Billing records reflect single charegs for each service rendered, with no duplicate
or repeated entries. Current status is improving, and the patient is expected to return to baseline function with
continued home exercise.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
